review_output.summary: The header declares isCosmeticVertex/isCosmeticEdge/isCenterLine as static and taking (App::DocumentObject* owner, std::string element), but DrawViewPart.cpp defines them as non-static members taking only (std::string element), so the signatures don't match.
review_output.failure_scenario: Building TechDraw fails with 'no declaration matches bool TechDraw::DrawViewPart::isCosmeticVertex(std::string)' (and the same for isCosmeticEdge and isCenterLine). If only the definitions were fixed, the static versions would have no 'this' and so could not call getEdge()/getProjVertexByIndex().

review_output.summary: CosmeticExtension::deleteCosmeticElements still calls DU::isCosmeticVertex, DU::isCosmeticEdge and DU::isCenterLine, which this change removes from DrawUtil; the call sites were not moved to getOwner()->isCosmeticVertex(name) and so on.
review_output.failure_scenario: CosmeticExtension.cpp fails to compile with 'isCosmeticVertex is not a member of TechDraw::DrawUtil' at lines 71, 77 and 78, which breaks the whole TechDraw App library.

review_output.summary: In the caller of the moved function, getCosmeticVertexBySelection(name) can return nullptr but its result is dereferenced without a check (the edge branch just below does check).
review_output.failure_scenario: A vertex is marked cosmetic but has no matching CosmeticVertex entry (for example stale geometry after a recompute, or a vertex created by another cosmetic source). vert is null and vert->getTagAsString() crashes FreeCAD when the user deletes the selection.

review_output.summary: The new member functions are not const and take std::string by value, even though they only call the const accessors getEdge()/getProjVertexByIndex().
review_output.failure_scenario: They cannot be called on a const DrawViewPart& (for example from toAppSpace-style helpers that take const DrawViewPart&), which invites const_cast. Every call also copies the string needlessly. They should be `bool isCosmeticVertex(const std::string& element) const` and so on.

review_output.summary: isCosmeticVertex repeats the existing DrawViewPart::getVertex(std::string) (getIndexFromName followed by getProjVertexByIndex) instead of calling it.
review_output.failure_scenario: The name-to-vertex lookup now exists in two places, so a future change to vertex naming or indexing must be made in both. The simpler form is `auto vertex = getVertex(element); return vertex && vertex->getCosmetic();`.

review_output.summary: isCosmeticEdge and isCenterLine are copy-pasted bodies that differ only in the SourceType value, and each uses the verbose `if (cond) return true; return false;` pattern.
review_output.failure_scenario: Duplicated logic that is harder to maintain. It could be one private helper, isCosmeticSource(element, SourceType), or at least `auto edge = getEdge(element); return edge && edge->source() == SourceType::CENTERLINE && edge->getCosmetic();`.

review_output.summary: The comments still read 'true if owner->element is ...', but the owner parameter no longer exists now that these are members.
review_output.failure_scenario: The stale comments point readers to a parameter that isn't there. They should say 'true if this view's element is ...'.

review_output.summary: The new geometry query declarations sit in the HLR/progress threading block (after waitingForResult/progressValueChanged) instead of next to the related getVertex/getEdge accessors around line 162.
review_output.failure_scenario: Related element-query APIs end up scattered across the header, which makes them harder to find. The declarations belong with getVertex/getEdge/getFace.
